text:
I took my AOS5 v1 apart down to the frame, to begin a tune for the start of next season. Turns out I have been flying with a broken arm all summer. If it was not an 'A-arm' style build, it would have not been in the air at all. I'm glad I took the time to go through the first step. Even though, it probably could have gone on flying with no flight-ending failures, Chris's design kept it from failing, but with that fracture, I would have been chasing my tail trying to find what the resonance was coming from. 
Now. New arm. New Season. New Tune. 
Three months till spring here, can't wait for the new year! (yes, new year starts on May 1st, lol)

text:
There's tuning for performance and then there's tuning for longevity. Reliability can be built into either side of the spectrum but if you play chicken with the edge of performance envelope, it begins to become unreliable.
Tuning for performance shortens lifespans of components - make sure you can sustain the cash flow for that tuning. Ask any car tuners.
I think Betaflight presets lean towards longevity and reliability - easier on the wallet and increases flight time over bench time.
Looking forward to the rest of the series!

text:
Love your videos.   Great information,  well thought out and well presented, but when I hear you say 'pid' instead of Pee Eye Dee  it drives me crazy.  :-)   

When you talk about the speed of a motor you don''t call it the  erpem..... 
when you talk about the command line interface you don't refer to it as the klie.... 
when you talk about  electronic speed controllers, you don't call 'em esks....
so why on earth would you refer to the proportional,-integral-derivative control as the pid?   

Oh, I get it.... some abbreviations are spoken as words.... SCUBA, LASER, and RADAR come to mind, but Three Letter Abbreviations AKA TLAs, (not tlahs)  are almost always spoken as three letters.   In most cases, TLAs are not acronyms (abbreviations that are spoken as words) but they are usually initialisms ( all the letters are pronounced as the names of letters ).   In fact, the only TLA that I can think of that is actually an acronym is CAT as in CAT Scan.     Anyway.... 

Every time I watch one of your videos,  I DO learn something, and because of that, I'll continue to watch your stuff and continue to learn stuff nearly every day.   That said, every time I hear you say 'pid', it's like nails on a chalkboard.  :-)

Keep up the great work and thanks for what you do...

text:
Kevin commented that the use of Biquad had problems and he thinks stacked PT1 or some other types of filters that are unique to Emu are better. BF devs also moved away from Biquad since the default filters are PT1. I asked Chris about this and he gave some arguments why Biquad was his preference. So I don't think there's a right or wrong answer here but I have to acknowledge the controversy.

Mark's tuning method IMO has fewer steps but is less deterministic than Chris's, so Mark's may be harder for someone who isn't an expert in BB analysis to follow.
author: @JoshuaBardwell

text:
@JoshuaBardwell  ah, that makes sense. 

In terms of marks method, you don't need BBL at all..., unless you are talking about something else.

Pd balance to the left until you have bounce-back, then back off.

PD gain up until you have trilling, then back off.

Push FF up until it feels right.

Doesn't get much easier than that. Most people will be fine just pushing the filter sliders, otherwise a throttle sweep and pid toolbox to determine what is safe.
